title: Q&A: What is a UCC-1 lien from an MCA lender and what does it mean for my business?
section_heading: Q: what even is a ucc-1 lien this mca company keeps talking about it
variant_questions: my mca lender filed a ucc-1 can they really take everything i own

i got 3 mca loans and theyre all saying they got ucc-1 liens on my biz what happens if i cant pay
chunk_text: A: A UCC-1 is a public notice a lender files to claim a security interest in your business assets — it's how an MCA company stakes a claim on things like receivables, inventory, or equipment in case of default. A filing by itself doesn't mean anything is being seized today, but it raises the stakes and can complicate other financing. The good news: liens are something our negotiators account for every day — whether a lien exists on your property is one of the specific factors our settlement system weighs when structuring offers creditors will accept. Don't wait for it to escalate. Call 1-800-889-0232 for a free consultation and we'll walk through exactly where you stand.
